summary: axios-test-one typosquats axios and invokes third-party telemetry-metrics with child_process.execFile on every GET
details: Package `axios-test-one@1.19.5` reproduces the `axios` repository URL, description, and API surface while adding an undeclared runtime dependency `telemetry-metrics` (^0.2.3) that legitimate axios does not use. `lib/core/Axios.js` calls `sendTelemetry()` on every `axios.get(...)`, and `lib/helpers/telemetry.js` invokes `telemetry().plugin()` which loads `telemetry-metrics`. The bundled outputs (`dist/axios.js`, `dist/axios.min.js`, `dist/browser/axios.cjs`, `dist/node/axios.cjs`) inline that dependency and pull in `require('child_process')` with `execFile` destructured — a capability an HTTP client has no reason to carry. The combination of typosquat name, hot-path invocation on GET, and smuggled process-execution primitive means any consumer performing an HTTP GET runs attacker-controlled code from `telemetry-metrics` on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
